items.title: native: a variant constructor of a ONE-parameter enum with a BOUNDED parameter is typed as a trait object: `enum Op<T: Hashable> { Add(T), Gone }` then `let op: Op<i32> = Op::Add(3);` → "a value of type `a trait object`"
items.body: With two parameters, or no bound, it builds. Blocks `SetCell`, `SetOp` and `MapCell::keys()` natively (refused by name today; kolt's `get_channels` stays a coarse derive for it). After the fix: flip `a138_map_and_set_cells_build_the_same_on_both_backends_or_are_refused_by_name` to identical. Sizing S–M; native lane, Order 46 FIRST.

items.title: native: `set(None)` on a two-parameter struct's `Signal<Option<V>>` impl → "unbound generic type parameter (parameter 2 of struct `Pair`)"
items.body: Repro: `struct Pair<K, V> { cell: SignalCell<Option<V>>, key: K }` implementing `Source`/`Signal<Option<V>>`; `pair.set(None)`. An annotated `None` binding builds (the workaround in maps-45's pins). Sizing S.

items.title: a STATIC trait call on a type bound only through an impl subject's NESTED binder raises an internal error: `N::default()` inside a method of `impl Stage<.., type R: IntoFlow<type N: Default>>` → "internal: a call resolved to `Default`'s requirement `default`, which has no body … please report"
items.body: Works when `N` is a direct impl parameter. Sizing M; solver.

items.title: `Source::get(x)` with no annotation does not infer the trait's `T` from the receiver: `Source::get(cell).keys()` → "cannot call method 'keys' on T"
items.body: It matters for `MapCell`: the inherent `get(key)` shadows the whole-map read on a concrete receiver, so the whole map is read as an annotated `Source::get(cell)` or `peek`. Rec: infer a qualified trait call's trait arguments from the receiver's impl. Sizing S–M; solver.
